title: Periprocedural myocardial infarction and injury
journal: European Heart Journal: Acute Cardiovascular Care
one_line_summary: Comprehensive state-of-the-art review summarizing the mechanisms, conflicting diagnostic criteria, prognostic impacts, and therapeutic mitigation strategies for periprocedural myocardial infarction and injury across coronary, valvular, and non-cardiac procedures.
key_pearls: **Periprocedural myocardial infarction (PMI)** occurs in **2%** to **15%** of coronary interventions (**PCI** and **CABG**), up to **14%** in **TAVI**, and **15%** in high-risk non-cardiac surgery.

Major diagnostic definitions vary markedly: the **4th UDMI** uses lower cardiac troponin (**cTn**) thresholds (**>5x URL** for PCI) with **mandatory** ancillary criteria, whereas **ARC-2** and **SCAI** enforce higher cut-offs (**>35x** or **>70x URL**).
Post-PCI major myocardial injury (defined as post-procedural **cTn >=5x 99th percentile URL**) is an independent predictor of **1-year all-cause mortality** regardless of assay sensitivity.

Myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (**MINS**) occurs in **~16%** of major general surgery cases; **>80%** of patients are asymptomatic due to perioperative analgesia, requiring routine postoperative **cTn** screening at **24** and **48 hours**.
The **MANAGE** trial established that initiating **dabigatran** in patients with **MINS** **significantly** reduces major vascular complications without **significantly** increasing major bleeding.

Pre-procedural administration of a **600 mg loading dose** of **clopidogrel** at least **2 hours** prior to elective PCI, or high-potency **prasugrel** or **ticagrelor**, **significantly** attenuates PMI risk.
population: Patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or non-cardiac surgical procedures.

sections.heading: Overview and Clinical Significance
sections.content:
- **Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)** and **coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG)** carry an incidence of periprocedural myocardial infarction (**PMI**) ranging between **~2%** and **~15%**.
- In non-coronary cardiac procedures such as **transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)**, **PMI** incidence approaches **14%**.
- High-risk patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery suffer **PMI** rates near **15%**.
- Differentiating **PMI** from isolated post-procedural **myocardial injury** (biomarker elevation without clinical or diagnostic signs of ischemia) remains an area of major clinical and investigative controversy.
section_pearls: Periprocedural death and stroke occur in **<3%** of revascularization cases, whereas **PMI** affects up to **15%**.

sections.heading: Pathophysiological Mechanisms across Procedural Modalities
sections.content:
- In the **PCI** setting, side-branch occlusion accounts for **~60%** of **PMI** cases, followed by distal coronary microembolization of thrombus or plaque debris (**10% - 15%**).
- Additional **PCI** causes include iatrogenic air embolization, acute stent thrombosis, coronary dissection, and mechanical vessel injury from plaque modification devices.
- In **CABG**, early graft failure causes up to **12%** of myocardial injuries (though only **~3%** are clinically evident) due to graft kinking, anastomosis stenosis, or graft thrombosis.
- Non-graft **CABG** causes include global hypoperfusion, inadequate cardioplegic protection, direct cardiac manipulation, reperfusion injury, and tachyarrhythmias.
- In **TAVI**, mechanisms encompass mechanical trauma from valve positioning or trans-apical access, calcific microembolization, rapid pacing-induced ischemia, and direct coronary ostial obstruction.
section_pearls: Side-branch occlusion is the primary driver of **PMI** during **PCI**, responsible for **60%** of events.

sections.heading: Diagnostic Definitions and Biomarker Criteria
sections.content:
- The **4th Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (UDMI)** defines **PCI-related myocardial injury** as **cTn** elevation **>1x 99th percentile URL** and **PMI** as **cTn >5x URL** plus **>=1 ancillary criteria** (new ECG ischemic changes, new Q waves, imaging proof of lost myocardium, or angiographic complications).
- **ARC-2** defines **PCI-related PMI** as **cTn >35x URL** with ancillary criteria, or **>70x URL** without ancillary criteria.
- **SCAI** primary criterion uses **CK-MB >10x URL** (or **cTn >70x URL**) standalone, or **CK-MB >5x URL** (or **cTn >35x URL**) with ancillary criteria.
- For **CABG**, **4th UDMI** requires **cTn >10x URL** plus ancillary criteria; **ARC-2** and **SCAI** require **cTn >35x URL** (with ancillary criteria) or **>70x URL** (standalone).
- For **TAVI**, **VARC-3** adopts **SCAI** and **ARC-2** standards (**CK-MB >=10x URL** or **cTn >=70x URL** standalone; **CK-MB >=5x URL** or **cTn >=35x URL** with ancillary criteria).
section_pearls: Biomarker threshold heterogeneity causes up to a **7-fold difference** in reported **PMI** rates across identical trial cohorts.

sections.heading: Prognostic Implications
sections.content:
- Minor periprocedural myocardial injury (**cTn 1-5x URL**) shows inconsistent correlation with long-term **mortality** across major trials.
- Major periprocedural injury (**cTn >=5x 99th percentile URL**) independently predicts **1-year all-cause mortality** across both conventional and high-sensitivity **cTn** assays.
- **PMI** defined by **ARC-2** or **SCAI** criteria occurs less frequently (**~2.0%** in chronic coronary syndromes) but carries higher specificity for predicting **1-year cardiac death** compared to **4th UDMI** (**14.9% - 18.0%** incidence).
- Following **TAVI**, **cTn** release **>70x URL** is strongly associated with increased **30-day** and **1-year mortality**.
section_pearls: Post-PCI **cTn** elevation **>=5x URL** represents the key prognostic inflection point for **1-year mortality**.

sections.heading: Risk Mitigation Strategies in PCI and Cardiac Surgery
sections.content:
- Pre-procedural identification of high-risk plaque features using **CCTA**, **CMR**, or **NIRS-IVUS** guides protective procedural planning.
- Pre-treatment with **clopidogrel 600 mg** loaded **>=2 hours** prior to elective **PCI** reduces **PMI** incidence.
- High-intensity **statin** reloading prior to **PCI** attenuates periprocedural tissue necrosis via pleiotropic anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
- Intra-procedural administration of intravenous **cangrelor** consistently decreases **48-hour PMI** rates across all diagnostic definitions.
- Intra-procedural intracoronary **enalaprilat** reduces microvascular resistance and lowers post-procedural **hs-cTnT** elevation.
- Surgical techniques such as the **no-touch technique** for vein graft harvesting and **internal mammary artery skeletonization** reduce surgical **PMI**.
section_pearls: Administering a **clopidogrel 600 mg** load at least **2 hours** before **PCI** optimizes antiplatelet inhibition and reduces **PMI**.

sections.heading: Myocardial Injury and Infarction in Non-Cardiac Surgery
sections.content:
- **Myocardial Injury after Non-cardiac Surgery (MINS)** is defined as ischemic myocardial injury (mismatch or thrombosis) occurring within **30 days** postoperatively without requiring non-ischemic triggers.
- **MINS** affects **~16%** of major surgical patients, increasing **30-day mortality** nearly **5-fold**.
- Over **80%** of **MINS** cases are completely asymptomatic due to routine postoperative opioid analgesia.
- Routine screening with **hs-cTn** at **24** and **48 hours** postoperatively is **recommended** (**Class I, Level B**) in high-risk non-cardiac surgery.
- The **MANAGE** trial demonstrated that initiating **dabigatran** (~6 days post-op) in patients with **MINS** **significantly** reduces major vascular complications, vascular **mortality**, and stroke.
section_pearls: Over **80%** of **MINS** episodes are clinically silent, making routine **24h/48h postoperative troponin screening** vital.

sections.heading: Clinical Trial Implications and Future Directions
sections.content:
- In the **EXCEL** trial, **PCI** was non-**inferior** to **CABG** using the protocol/SCAI **PMI** definition (**3.6% vs 6.1%**), but **CABG** was **superior** when using **3rd UDMI** criteria (**2.2% vs 4.0%**).
- In the **SYNTAX** trial, switching from **SCAI** to **4th UDMI** expanded **CABG-related PMI** rates from **2.1%** to **16.5%**, shifting overall trial primary endpoints.
- Future diagnostic refinements focus on machine-learning-driven personalized biomarker cut-offs, novel dual-marker rule-out strategies combining **copeptin** and **hs-cTn**, and standardizing non-troponin angiographic/ECG ancillary criteria.
section_pearls: Trial conclusions comparing **PCI** vs **CABG** can flip entirely depending on whether **SCAI** or **UDMI** definitions for **PMI** are chosen.

strengths_limitations:
- Strengths: Comprehensive synthesized analysis covering cardiac revascularization, structural interventions (TAVI), and non-cardiac surgical spectrums; detailed comparison of diagnostic definitions across all major cardiology consortia (ESC, ACC, AHA, SCAI, ARC-2, VARC-3).
- Limitations: Broad narrative structure limits quantitative meta-analytic pooling; lack of uniform international consensus on standardized cut-offs complicates clear clinical algorithmic mandates.
